brief: A caddy that holds two jerry cans of petrol upright in the boot of my car.

requirements.evidence: Nothing placed. No caddy was built because restraining jerry cans in a moving vehicle cannot be verified safe in 3D-printed plastic with fit-only checks.
requirements.requirement: Caddy that holds two jerry cans

requirements.evidence: Nothing placed. Upright restraint during driving would need load, crash and restraint verification the configurator does not do.
requirements.requirement: Holds cans upright in the boot of a car

requirements.evidence: Declined as unsafe as asked: holds fuel (petrol). The parts are 3D-printed plastic and the configurator checks fit only, with no knowledge of fuel resistance, heat, strength or crash safety.

finish.summary: Declined - placed nothing. A 3D-printed caddy cannot safely restrain two petrol jerry cans upright in a car boot; fuel containment and in-vehicle restraint need rated hardware the configurator cannot verify. I can build a static storage caddy for empty cans or workshop use instead if wanted.
